newsitem.title: USA: Dow falls 93 points in broad pullback by US stocks.
newsitem.headline: Dow falls 93 points in broad pullback by US stocks.

text.p: Wall Street stocks finished broadly lower on Thursday, as interest rates edged higher for the second straight day and investors cashed in on some gains from the market's sizzling rally.

The Dow industrials fell 93 points to close unofficially at 6927. Broader indices and market breadth also turned decidedly weaker amid the first concerted profit-taking since the Dow cracked 7000 late last week.
"We've had day after day of stocks going up," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"Now it appears some money managers are taking some chips off the table in the best performing groups," he said.

Technology and financial stocks met with some of the stiffest selling pressure, with the latter under extra pressure from an ongoing decline in the bond market that has pushed the long bond's yield up to 6.65 percent.
At the same time, tech stocks turned in a particularly choppy performance, even when compared with an overall market that displays increasing volatility by the day.

"We're in a stage of the market where volatility is going to remain quite high," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon and Farrell. "There is a broad variety of opinions being expressed by market observers and at any given moment one camp will gain an upper hand."
"In technology, there may be the greatest degree of controversy about the profit outlook," he added.
International Business Machines Corp fell 2-5/8 to 141, Intel Corp shed four to 149-7/8 and Microsoft Corp dipped 2-1/4 to 95-1/4.

Shares in gold and silver mining companies managed to buck the trend, buoyed by a sharp rise in precious metal prices. Newmont Mining Corp gained 1-7/8 to 46-1/8, Barrick Gold Corp rose 3/4 to 26-7/8 and Coeur D'Alene Mines Corp jumped 1-1/4 to 18-1/8.
The session also saw the dollar retreat a bit from its sizable gains, falling against both the Japanese yen and German mark.
The dollar's strength has been an important factor in the stock market's rally, because it has drawn considerable investment to U.S. financial markets from outside the country.

With the stock market still near all-time high levels, the possibility that ebbing dollar strength and slower mutual fund contributions, which dip seasonally after January, could spell more trouble for stocks, analysts said.

"The belief is that perhaps stocks may be entering into a period of correction for a while," said Harry Laubscher, a market analyst at Tucker Anthony. "The market has been looking kind of toppy lately."
Shares in energy companies dipped as world oil prices fell to six-month lows. Mobil Corp fell two points to 128-1/4, and Chevron Corp fell 1-5/8 to 65-5/8.

Brokerage stocks were weaker after Oppenheimer & Co downgraded 10 companies in the sector, saying sharp price appreciation had reduced the group's attractiveness. Among those cut were PaineWebber Group Inc, which fell two to 34-7/8, and A.G. Edwards Inc, off 2-3/8 to 37-3/8.

Cyrix Corp jumped 3-7/8 to 29-3/8 after news that it would supply Compaq Computer Corp with a microprocessor for use in a new-low cost computer line. Compaq fell 2-3/4 to 82-5/8 amid widespread declines by tech stocks.
The S&P 500 index fell 9.69 to 802.80.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 18.18 to 1347.40.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
